name: IPW-XFWL Impact Xtreme, 27 September 2003

appearances.note: Brought Razor to the ring and was thrown into the steel steps by Roadkill after the match.
Walked to ringside during Killmore's match with Venom and was attacked by Venom.
A backstage segment with fellow Future members Lance and Paul.
A comedic backstage vignette with Molly Ringwald's Boyfriend.
Picked one of two ten-man War Games teams for the following week's Fallout, alongside Bob Munroe.
Interrupted the War Games team selection to insert himself into the match.
Appeared live via satellite from Japan and was attacked on camera by three wrestlers wearing Caramel t-shirts.
Confronted Max and arranged a singles match at Funhouse.

matches.note: A tag match with individualized stakes: whoever scored the winning pin earned a title shot the following week. Bouncer pinned Frenzy after a No Remorse pedigree, earning his choice of the E-Championship or Junior Heavyweight Championship.
Igor pinned Homer after a series of chokeslams.
Roadkill won with a steel-chain punch, then assaulted Razor's cornerman Chester McDoogle after the bell.
Venom accused Killmore of winning only because D Money's ringside presence distracted him, and attacked Killmore with a Pancake Piledriver after the match.
Hurrikat attacked Peaches with a chair as the bell rang and was disqualified.
Peaches won the gauntlet despite a back injury sustained earlier in the series, becoming number-one contender for the Women's Championship.

notes: The broadcast's own cold open recaps an angle among Max, Tyrant, and Caramel from the previous week's show, not itself served in the held record. Joey Gots and Bob Munroe also picked the ten-man lineup for the following week's War Games match at Fallout; neither Fallout nor War Games survives as a served document in the held record.

name: IPW-XFWL Hardcore Holiday

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline (a Sunday-night pay-per-view).

appearances.note: Bit two of the North Pole Street Fight's competitors during the match.
Joined Big Daddy Cool Dudley at ringside after the Iron Man match.
Confiscated the Tag Team Championship belts amid the disputed finish, was fired and then rehired by Joey Gots, and declared the title vacant pending a January tournament.
Conducted a backstage interview with JuggaØ.
Interfered twice on Psyklone's behalf during his match with Spindle.
Applauded 411's title win from the stage after the match.

matches.stipulation: Two out of Three Falls, for the IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Mark won the first fall by pinfall; Venom won the second by a small-package rollup; Venom won the deciding third fall by submission (Dragon Clutch) to become new champion.
A six-man weapons brawl staged around Christmas-themed set pieces; Killmore pinned Frenzy with a piledriver (Cix Times The Pain).

matches.stipulation: Chain Match, for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship
matches.note: Both competitors' shoulders were down at once; two referees counted simultaneous pinfalls for opposite sides, and the finish was never resolved on air. The promotion's own authority figure Scout confiscated the belts and later declared the title vacant.
Big Daddy Cool Dudley won four falls to three, the deciding pinfall landing with two seconds left on the clock.

matches.stipulation: Nightmare Before Christmas Match (barbwire ropes, thumbtacks, and a burning table)
matches.note: Phoenix extinguished a burning table before Spindle could drive Psyklone through it, then knocked Spindle out with a loaded boot; Psyklone won with the Cloning Device through a second burning table.

matches.stipulation: Triangle Turbulence, for the IPW-XFWL E-Championship
matches.note: The match's own rule required Roadkill to pin Bouncer, Bouncer to pin Hazzard, and Hazzard to pin Roadkill to win. Bouncer instead climbed onto a pin Roadkill was making on champion Hazzard; the referee counted the fall and the ring announcer declared Bouncer the new champion regardless of the stated rule.
Max appeared to have the match won after escaping his own stretcher to attack Caramel, but a diving frog splash off the top rope missed and Max was counted out on his own stretcher instead.

matches.stipulation: Bring Your Own Weapon Match, for the IPW-XFWL World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Fought partly in and around a car in the parking lot; 411 pinned defending champion Tyrant to become new champion.

notes: An eight-part pay-per-view transcript, posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy in eight separate messages the same day; each part is served as its own page under this wing's archive.

name: IPW-XFWL Fallout featuring War Games

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline (a special Saturday-night television event).

appearances.note: Attacked new Women's Champion Peaches from behind after the title match and stole the championship belt.
Ambushed White Shadow at ringside with Igor Maskarow after their tag title match.
Ambushed White Shadow at ringside with Pawel Trojakow after their tag title match.
Told Tyrant he had hired a man to take out 411; nearly attacked by 411 after War Games before Everest's debut.
Produced a contract he said D Money had signed for a match at Funhouse; D Money denied signing it.
Denied signing Killmore's contract for a Funhouse match, calling it a forgery.
Also seen backstage warning Joey Gots against interfering on his behalf.
Wrestling as the masked "Lions".
Nearly attacked Joey Gots after the match before Everest's debut chokeslam stopped him.
Emerged from beneath the ring after War Games and chokeslammed 411 through the mat, debuting as Joey Gots's hired gun.

matches.note: Bouncer was knocked unconscious outside the ring after a chair shot and a collision with the guardrail; the referee stopped the match without declaring a winner, and Hazzard kept the title.
Peaches won the title with a Texas Cloverleaf submission.

matches.stipulation: For the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The Future retained after Lance rolled through a Bobby White sunset flip attempt for the pin.
Max choked Spindle out with a steel chain to win. The match was billed as Joey Gots's own hand-picked team against a squad assembled around John Norvilas.

notes: Killmore's contract angle with D Money and the debut of Joey Gots's hired gun Everest, who chokeslammed 411 through the ring after War Games ended, both carried forward into later broadcasts.

name: IPW-XFWL Impact Xtreme, 11 October 2003

appearances.note: Accompanied The Two Dudes to the ring.
Returned from his on-air coma to make the save on The Funk Master and challenge Roadkill to a No Limits match at Funhouse.
Interfered with a ring-bell shot to help Frenzy win.
Guest commentator for the Firestrike/Frenzy match; announced a four-way Junior Heavyweight title defense at Funhouse against Firestrike, Frenzy, and J-Sleazy.
Wrestling as "Lions"; made the save on the Incredible Edible Kid after Spindle's post-match chair beating, then accepted a mask-on-the-line match against Spindle for Funhouse.
Accepted the mask-on-the-line stipulation on Lions's behalf without consulting him.
Challenged White Shadow to a match, booked by Scout for the following week.
Challenged White Shadow to a match, booked by Scout for the following week.
Accepted The Russians' challenge; Scout booked the match for the following week.
Accepted The Russians' challenge; Scout booked the match for the following week.
Booked The Russians against White Shadow, and set stipulation matches for The Future's own Two Dudes rematch, both for the following week.
Also announced that Caramel would face 411 the following week.
Interfered on Yoshihiro Toyama's behalf; matched up against Max at Funhouse.
Interfered on Yoshihiro Toyama's behalf, distracting the referee; introduced as Pride's newest member and Caramel's wife.
Came to the ring with the stolen Women's Championship belt and was confronted by Peaches, who challenged her to a match at Funhouse.
Confronted Amanda Clark over the stolen Women's Championship and challenged her to a match at Funhouse.
Mocked the previous week's E-Championship match in a video segment, then had Joey Gots sign a three-way E-Championship match against Hazzard and Bouncer for Funhouse.
Introduced Everest live and announced a 411 vs. Everest match for Funhouse.
Appeared live with Joey Gots, who announced a singles match against 411 at Funhouse.
Brought a toy championship belt as a mocking "gift" for John Norvilas, then was busted open in the resulting chair attack.
Attacked Tyrant with a chair after being mocked with a toy title belt, stopped only when Living Dead Girl came to Tyrant's aid.
Ran in to stop John Norvilas's chair attack on her boyfriend Tyrant.
Asked Scout to make the following week's Two Dudes rematch non-title if The Future won two singles matches first.
Asked Scout to make the following week's Two Dudes rematch non-title if The Future won two singles matches first.
An FBI handwriting expert confirmed his signature was genuine on Killmore's contract, keeping their Funhouse match on.
His contract with D Money was confirmed genuine by an FBI handwriting expert, keeping their Funhouse match on.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contender's match for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The Two Dudes won and earned a title shot at Funhouse.
Roadkill won with a Chokebomb, then continued beating down Funk Master after the bell until Rex made his surprise return.
Frenzy pinned Firestrike after J-Sleazy ran in and struck Firestrike with the ring bell.
Spindle won with a DDT, then continued the beating with a chair until Lions ran in for the save.
Toyama won after spitting green mist in Max's face, with Pride's Caramel and The Hurrikat interfering throughout.

notes: Opens with a recap of the previous week's War Games finish, not itself re-served here.

name: IPW-XFWL Funhouse II

appearances.note: Accompanied The Two Dudes to the ring.
Ran in to help The Future retain the tag titles against The Two Dudes.
Interfered on D Money's behalf and was ejected from ringside by the referee.
Ran in with a Gore on Roadkill to help Rex win the No Limits match; also appeared in a taped vignette attacking a Santa Claus figure to promote the upcoming Hardcore Holiday pay-per-view.
Also seen backstage with Joey Gots and Everest before his own match.

Wrestling as the masked "Lions"; lost to Spindle by disqualification after his own manager Bob Munroe struck Spindle with a chair, then was unmasked on Joey Gots's order, revealed as JuggaO, and finished the night by planting Tyrant with a Juggabomb.
Struck Spindle with a chair, costing Lions the match by disqualification and the mask that followed.
Interviewed Bob Munroe about the Spindle/Lions mask stipulation.
Retained the World Championship, then was attacked and hit with a Juggabomb by the newly-unmasked JuggaO.
Sent Spindle, Tyrant, and Everest into their matches, then ordered Lions to unmask after Spindle's win.

matches.stipulation: For the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The Future retained after Kevin J. Ridge ran in to help finish The Two Dudes.
Killmore won by pinning D Money face-first into D Money's own briefcase, settling their forged-contract feud.

matches.stipulation: Four-way, one fall to a finish, for the IPW-XFWL Junior Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Mark Prohibition retained, pinning J-Sleazy with the Burning Hammer.
A brawl through the parking lot and back to the ring; Razor ran in with a Gore on Roadkill to let Rex get the pin.
Hazzard retained, escaping a Kevin J. Ridge cover in time to pin Bouncer.
Spindle won by disqualification after Lions's own manager Bob Munroe struck Spindle with a chair; Lions was unmasked afterward on Joey Gots's order and revealed as JuggaO.
The Russians won after Igor pinned Bobby White following a top-rope splash.
Peaches forced the match after Amanda Clark tried to cancel it, then retained with a standing shooting star press.
Max won with an Ace Crusher off the middle rope.
411 pinned Everest after hitting his own Spinechoppa finisher on the much larger man.

matches.stipulation: Rage In The Cage (steel cage), for the IPW-XFWL World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Both men crashed through the cage roof to the canvas; Tyrant landed a hand on John Norvilas for the pin.

notes: Closes with Lions unmasked as JuggaO, a former XFWL owner, who plants champion Tyrant with a Juggabomb and escapes through the crowd.

name: IPW-XFWL Impact Xtreme, 18 October 2003

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline; posted in three parts the same week.

notes: A three-part weekly broadcast transcript, posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy in three separate messages; each part is served as its own page under this wing's archive. Part 3 closes on an angle (411's chair-shot confrontation with Everest) with no bell rung, not a scored match.

appearances.note: Accompanied Caramel to ringside and climbed onto the ring apron to distract the referee.
Accompanied Caramel to ringside; shoved into 411 by Caramel during the chase.
Watched Frenzy's post-match attack on Firestrike from the entranceway and declined to make the save, drawing commentary criticism ahead of his four-way Junior Heavyweight defense at Funhouse.
Entered the ring illegally and attacked the referee and both members of White Shadow, drawing the disqualification; Scout overturned the result to a no-contest and signed a Funhouse rematch.
Took a rigged lie-detector test attempting to prove he never signed his Funhouse contract against Killmore; the test read his denial as a lie and he confirmed the match instead.
Named as D Money's Funhouse opponent; not shown on camera this episode.
Interfered at ringside on Lance's behalf, distracting the referee and tripping Molly Ringwald's Boyfriend.
Ran in to help Big Daddy Cool Dudley against Kevin J. Ridge's interference, drawing a rebuke from Avery Rogers on commentary.
Confronted by a chair-wielding 411 in the closing segment; the two brawled to a stalemate with no bell rung before Everest military-pressed and launched 411 into the ring post.
Named on commentary as Everest's employer, paying him to take 411 out ahead of Funhouse.

matches.note: 411 no-sold a self-inflicted chair shot by Caramel (meant for 411, it bounced off the top rope back into Caramel's own head) and finished with a spinechoppa.
Firestrike won with a shooting star press (his "Hearts Of Fire") after a plancha to the floor took out an interfering Frenzy.

White Shadow won by disqualification when Igor entered illegally and attacked the referee, but Scout, the promotion's director of decisions, overturned the finish to a no-contest on the grounds White Shadow had been double-teaming Pawel; a rematch was signed for Funhouse.

Part of The Future's own tag-title defense stipulation: winning both of two singles matches against the Two Dudes this episode would make the Funhouse tag title match non-title. Lance won with a Future Shock (powerbomb/neckbreaker combo) after Kevin J. Ridge's ringside interference.

The Two Dudes' other qualifier for a title shot at Funhouse. BDCD won with a Dragonrana after Hazzard ran in to even the numbers against Kevin J. Ridge's interference; since only one of the two Future qualifiers was won, the Funhouse tag match remained for the title.

appearances.note: Opened the show unmasked for the first time under his own name (his mask-loss as "Lions" at Funhouse having already outed him), challenged Joey Gots directly, and vanished mid-promo in a pyro explosion after a demonic voice said "THRYCE".
Booked JuggaØ and a partner of his choosing against Tyrant and Everest for the following week after JuggaØ's challenge.
Named as one half of the following week's tag match against JuggaØ and Akira.
Named as Tyrant's partner for the following week's tag match.
Named by JuggaØ as his partner for the following week, described as a former tag partner of Everest; did not appear in person.

Thanked the Funk Master backstage for challenging Roadkill on his behalf, then was pulled away by a technician to see a second threatening message (a photo of himself with a knife through it, signed "Rex").
Ambushed Killmore from the crowd before the bell; lost anyway.
Interfered with a chair for Toyama, then tried a low blow on the victorious Max, only to be caught; Caramel made the save.
Attacked Max after the bell with a steel chair and then a crowbar to the ribs and nose, ending the segment with Max stretchered out.
Billed as a non-title defense of his E-Championship, per his own successful title defense against Bouncer and Kevin J. Ridge six days earlier.
Accompanied Razor and helped set up weapons for the No Limits main event.

matches.note: Dante, a new masked wrestling monk under a vow of silence, teamed with Firestrike; Dante pinned Frenzy with a shooting star press after Firestrike's German suplex.
Killmore's second straight win over a veteran, by spinning powerbomb, after Spindle ambushed him from the crowd before the bell.
Max blocked a mist attempt with a steel chair Hurrikat had slid him and finished with an Ace Crusher; PRIDE beat Max down after the bell, closing with Caramel breaking his nose with a crowbar.
Bouncer won with Hazzard's own No Remorse pedigree after Roadkill ran in and chokeslammed Hazzard onto a chair on the outside during the match.
A ladder/tables brawl; Roadkill won by dumping Razor off a ladder through two stacked tables.

appearances.note: Challenged anyone in the building to a match, then fled the ring when Psyklone answered the challenge from the stage without a word.
Returned after over a year away, silently answering Spindle's open challenge and sending him running.

Defended her self-purchased "Real" Women's Championship, a belt bought with her own inheritance and not recognized by the promotion as the real Women's Championship; the broadcast's own color commentator announced the win from ringside as "still the Real Women's Champion."
Wrestling under his own name for the first time this collection, alongside Akira.
Turned on Tyrant mid-match, chokeslamming him instead of Akira and revealing himself as a third member of the new faction "Thryce" alongside JuggaØ and Akira.
Discussed an investor pulling out of the company with Cousin Vinny; confronted by D Money over the pullout.
Implied he used his business connections to cost Joey Gots an investor.
Joey Gots' cousin; delivered the news that Pepsi had pulled its advertising from the show.
Returned from a tour of Japan as Kevin J. Ridge's team's mystery fourth man, still billed as the JAW Junior Weight Triple Crown champion.

matches.stipulation: number-one contender's match for the IPW-XFWL Tag Team Championship
matches.note: The Russians won with a top-rope moonsault after a big splash/moonsault combo, becoming the number-one contenders.
Pimpslap (Rex and The Funk Master, a new pairing) won with a simultaneous double pin after their own double-team finisher ("Hardcore Rex" DDT into a Funkenator).

matches.stipulation: for Amanda Clark's self-declared "Real" Women's Championship
matches.note: Amanda's first defense of the title she bought with her own money; won with a foreign object (a roll of coins) against a Japanese wrestler billed as Big Van Driver.

No finish: Everest chokeslammed Tyrant instead of Akira mid-match, then he, JuggaØ and Akira (a bribed referee having conveniently left) beat Tyrant down and unveiled themselves as the new faction Thryce; no bell, no decision.

matches.stipulation: eight-man MegaCard Combat match (no count-outs, no disqualifications, no tags necessary, one fall to a finish); the winning captain would draw the stipulation for Kevin J. Ridge's own rematch against Big Daddy Cool Dudley at Hardcore Holiday, and the winning side split a $20,000 prize
matches.note: Kevin J. Ridge pinned Big Daddy Cool Dudley with a top-rope Ridged Rupture to win it for his team.

appearances.note: Signed 411 vs. Tyrant for the World Title and Tyrant vs. JuggaØ, both for the following weeks, then took a spinechoppa from 411 after ordering him out of the building.
Stood with JuggaØ and Everest as Thryce, taunting 411 backstage.
Brawled with Peaches in the women's locker room; Scout booked their own "Real" vs. real Women's Championship dispute into a ladder match at Hardcore Holiday.
Took a charging Gore meant for Firestrike, re-injuring his neck.
Challenged the Russians to earn a tag title shot against a team of The Future's own choosing the following week.
Part of PRIDE's post-match beatdown of Killmore, broken up by Pimpslap.
Ran in with Funk Master to clear PRIDE out of the ring.
Demanded Joey Gots add Bouncer to his own E-Championship match after Bouncer attacked him backstage; Joey obliged.
Ambushed Roadkill backstage with a chair, then a pedigree onto the steel.
Told Roadkill even monsters have weaknesses shortly before Bouncer's ambush.
Drew a sixty-minute Iron Man match, IPW-XFWL's first, against Kevin J. Ridge for Hardcore Holiday from Scout's envelope.
Dressed as a fake referee at Spindle's request, fast-counting a JuggaØ pin attempt on Spindle before being tossed from the ring; had earlier told Joey a Pepsi ad pullout was the extent of his news.

matches.note: Heather Sever's debut. Peaches won with a schoolgirl rollup after Heather's own gorilla press held on too long.
Taurus's debut, wrestling thirty pounds over his own stated Junior Heavyweight target weight. Firestrike won with a shooting star press after Chester McDoogle took a Gore meant for him.
Killmore won with a piledriver after Caramel cheated repeatedly, including an illegal ring-post figure-four leglock the referee eventually broke up.

A hardcore-leaning main event with chairs, a fake referee (Cousin Vinny, at Spindle's own request) fast-counting a near-fall, and Psyklone running in to attack Spindle before JuggaØ's own referee recovered to make the winning count.

appearances.note: Lumberjack for PRIDE; pulled Killmore out of the ring.
Spit green mist in Killmore's eyes to set up Caramel's cheap win.
Lumberjack for Killmore, alongside two unnamed valets billed as "the Funkette's."
Returned from injury to ambush Caramel with a chair and a top-rope leg drop through it, ending the segment with Caramel stretchered out.
Booked a six-man North Pole Street Fight (PRIDE vs. Killmore/Pimpslap) and a Max vs. Caramel stretcher match for Hardcore Holiday.
Ran in to make the save for MRB after Kevin exposed a turnbuckle.
Introduced "Lance and Storm" as The Future's own chosen opponent for the Russians, only for Lance and Paul themselves to wrestle the match.
Cornered 411 for the World Title match; shoved Joey Gots down at ringside.
Cornered Tyrant; handed him brass knuckles and later pulled the referee out of the ring twice to protect the title.
Ran in during the World Title match to chair Tyrant, causing the referee to call for the bell with no decision.

matches.note: Caramel stole a schoolboy pin (with a handful of tights) after Yoshihiro Toyama blinded Killmore with green mist.
Molly Ringwald's Boyfriend won by disqualification when Kevin exposed a turnbuckle and drove MRB's head into the exposed steel; Kevin then beat MRB down until Big Daddy Cool Dudley made the save.

matches.stipulation: non-title; the Russians would earn a tag title shot at Hardcore Holiday if they won
matches.note: The Russians won when Igor hit a top-rope splash on Paul after Paul had already used a title belt as a weapon; the Russians earned the right to pick the Hardcore Holiday title match's own gimmick.
Phoenix won with a top-rope skytwister press ("Hong Kong Skyline") after avoiding a Banzai Drop.

matches.stipulation: for the IPW-XFWL World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: No decision: 411 had Tyrant covered for what would have been the title change when JuggaØ ran in and chaired Tyrant; the referee, having lost control of the match, called for the bell with no winner declared. Tyrant retained by default.
